extracted.intended_audience: public housing agencies (PHAs), project owners, responsible entities, HUD staff, and tenants/tenant counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules (24 CFR part 5) governing hearings, preservation assistance (continued, temporary deferral, prorated), proration calculations across HUD programs, nondiscrimination, liability, and numerous defined terms for Section 8, public housing, and other HUD-assisted programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family hearing rights (presentation and confrontation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The family shall be entitled to present evidence relied upon by the responsible entity and to confront and cross-examine all witnesses on whose testimony or information the responsible entity relies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph enumerates core due-process hearing rights: to present evidence and to confront/cross-examine witnesses whose testimony the responsible entity uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation at hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The family shall be entitled to be represented by an attorney, or other designee, at the family's expense, and to have such person make statements on the family's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation is at the family's expense; designees may make statements for the family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive services at hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The family shall be entitled to arrange for an interpreter to attend the hearing, at the expense of the family, or responsible entity, as may be agreed upon by the two parties to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreter cost allocation is by agreement; family may arrange an interpreter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing recording
rubrics_metrics.description: The family shall be entitled to have the hearing recorded by audiotape (a transcript of the hearing may, but is not required to, be provided by the responsible entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible entity need not provide a transcript; audiotape recording at family's option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing decision timing and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible entity shall provide the family with a written final decision, based solely on the facts presented at the hearing, within 14 days of the date of the informal hearing. The decision shall state the basis for the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision must be written, fact-based, explain basis, and issued within 14 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial relief preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision against a family member, issued in accordance with paragraphs (e) or (f) of this section, does not preclude the family from exercising the right, that may otherwise be available, to seek redress directly through judicial procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative adverse decision does not eliminate judicial remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document retention by responsible entity
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible entity shall retain for a minimum of 5 years specified documents submitted or provided as part of the INS appeal or informal hearing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of required retained documents: application for financial assistance; form completed for income reexamination; photocopies of any original documents (front/back); signed verification consent form; INS verification results; request for INS appeal; final INS determination; request for informal hearing; final informal hearing decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of assisted occupancy methods (Housing programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Housing covered programs, and in Section 8 covered programs (other than Voucher and Moderate Rehab), assisted occupancy is terminated by: (i) if permitted under the lease, responsible entity notifying tenant that tenant must pay HUD-approved market rent; (ii) responsible entity and tenant entering into a new lease without financial assistance; or (iii) responsible entity evicting the tenant (eviction must be promptly initiated and diligently pursued according to lease and judicial action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While tenant remains in occupancy, assistance payments may continue if eviction action is promptly initiated and diligently pursued; HUD may set maximum periods for continued payments during eviction and standards of reasonable diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of assisted occupancy methods (Voucher & Moderate Rehab)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Section 8 Rental Voucher and Moderate Rehabilitation programs, assisted occupancy is terminated by terminating assistance payments. After required procedures are completed, PHA shall not make additional assistance payments, approve a lease, enter into an assistance contract, or process a portability move for the family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination is effected by stopping payments; PHAs must not take further assistance-related actions after termination procedures are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation assistance types available to mixed families
rubrics_metrics.description: Three types of preservation assistance are available to tenant mixed families following completion of appeals and informal hearing procedures: (i) Continued assistance; (ii) Temporary deferral of termination of assistance; (iii) Prorated assistance (a mixed family must be provided prorated assistance if requested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability depends on program and family eligibility; continued assistance is mandatory if conditions met for Housing covered programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of assistance by program (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Housing covered programs: one of the three types is available depending on family's eligibility; continued assistance must be provided to a mixed family that meets the conditions. For Section 8 or Public Housing programs: one of the three types may be available; PHAs have discretion but must offer prorated assistance to eligible mixed families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs must establish policy and criteria for granting continued assistance or temporary deferral and must incorporate statutory criteria in §5.518.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prorated assistance availability for applicant mixed families
rubrics_metrics.description: Prorated assistance is also available for mixed families applying for assistance as provided in §5.520.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who qualify as mixed families may request and receive prorated assistance per proration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary deferral availability to other families in occupancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary deferral of termination of assistance may be available to families receiving assistance under a Section 214 covered program on June 19, 1995, who have no members with eligible immigration status, as specified for Housing and Section 8/Public Housing covered programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible entity may grant deferral per applicable program-specific rules described in §5.518(c)(1)-(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion for project owners and PHAs on preservation assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: For Section 8 Act covered programs administered by a project owner, HUD has discretion to determine circumstances for providing continued assistance or temporary deferral; HUD specifies standards project owners must follow. For PHAs, the PHA (not HUD) has discretion but must establish policy and criteria incorporating statutory criteria; PHAs must offer prorated assistance to eligible families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project owners follow HUD-prescribed standards; PHAs set local policy consistent with statutory criteria in §5.518(a) and (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued assistance eligibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A mixed family may receive continued housing assistance if all of the following are met: (i) family was receiving assistance under a Section 214 covered program on June 19, 1995; (ii) head of household or spouse has eligible immigration status as described in §5.506; (iii) family does not include any person (without eligible status) other than head, spouse, parents of head/spouse, or children of head/spouse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housing covered program mixed family that meets these three conditions must be provided continued assistance; later-entitled families may be subject to proration rules (§5.520).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration of continued assistance based on date
rubrics_metrics.description: A family entitled to continued assistance before November 29, 1996 is entitled to continued assistance as described; a family entitled after November 29, 1996 shall receive prorated assistance as described in §5.520.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal cutoff affects whether full continued assistance or proration applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for temporary deferral of termination of assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mixed family qualifies for prorated assistance (and does not accept it), or if a family has no members with eligible immigration status, the family may be eligible for temporary deferral of termination of assistance if necessary to permit time for orderly transition to other affordable housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Other affordable housing’ is defined as non-substandard, appropriately sized housing that can be rented for an amount not exceeding the family's current rent (including utilities) plus 25 percent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions requiring grant of temporary deferral (Housing covered programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entity shall grant temporary deferral to a mixed family assisted under a Housing covered program if one of the following is met: (i) family demonstrates reasonable efforts to find other affordable housing have been unsuccessful (reasonable efforts include pursuing leads from State housing agency, city government, newspapers, rental agencies, owner); (ii) vacancy rate for affordable housing of appropriate size is below five percent in the relevant housing market; (iii) consolidated plan indicates lack of sufficient affordable housing opportunities for similar households.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three alternative tests — evidence of unsuccessful search, vacancy rate <5%, or consolidated plan showing inadequate supply — any of which supports deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits on temporary deferral periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial deferral period not to exceed six months; may be renewed for additional six-month periods but aggregate deferral after Nov 29, 1996 shall not exceed 18 months. Aggregate deferral prior to Nov 29, 1996 shall not exceed 3 years. These time periods do not apply to families including a refugee (INA §207) or asylum seeker (INA §208).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different aggregate ceilings apply depending on date of grant; refugees/asylees exempt from these time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification at beginning of each deferral period
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of each deferral period, the responsible entity must inform the family of its ineligibility for financial assistance and offer information and referrals to assist in finding other affordable housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible entity must provide active assistance information when deferral begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of availability of affordable housing at end of deferral period
rubrics_metrics.description: Before end of each deferral period, responsible entity must satisfy either (A) for Housing covered programs: determine one of §5.518(b)(2) conditions continues to be met (vacancy rate >=5% means housing available) or owner's knowledge and tenant's evidence indicate availability; or (B) for Section 8/Public Housing: determine availability based on combined evidence: consolidated plan (if applicable), responsible entity's knowledge, and tenant family's efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible entity must evaluate and document availability; different evidentiary approaches for Housing vs Section 8/Public Housing programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 60‑day written notice before deferral expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entity must notify tenant family in writing at least 60 days in advance of expiration of deferral whether (A) termination will be deferred again (provided aggregate max not exceeded), or (B) termination will not be deferred because another deferral would exceed aggregate maximum or because other affordable housing is available. The 60‑day notice does not apply to families including refugees/asylees when a determination was made that housing is not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice must explain outcome and is timed at least 60 days before expiration (subject to refugee/asylee exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to select proration at end of deferral period
rubrics_metrics.description: A family eligible for and receiving temporary deferral may request, and the responsible entity shall provide, proration of assistance at the end of the deferral period if the family has made a good faith effort during the deferral to locate other affordable housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good faith housing search during deferral creates right to proration upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of decision on family preservation assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: A responsible entity shall notify the family of its decision concerning qualification for family preservation assistance. If ineligible, the notification shall state the reasons, which must be based on relevant factors. For tenant families, notice shall inform of any applicable appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must state relevant reasons and advise of appeal rights for tenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of proration (§5.520)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section applies to mixed families other than those receiving continued assistance or those who request/receive temporary deferral. An eligible mixed family who requests prorated assistance must be provided prorated assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proration is mandatory upon request for eligible mixed families not receiving continued or deferral assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method — Rent Supplement Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Rent supplement paid shall be the rent supplement the household would otherwise be entitled to multiplied by a fraction: numerator = number of eligible persons in household; denominator = total number of people in household.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple fraction based on eligible persons shares the otherwise-applicable supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method — Section 235 Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest reduction payments shall be the payments the household would otherwise be entitled to multiplied by a fraction: numerator = eligible persons; denominator = total persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same fractional method as Rent Supplement applied to interest reduction payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method — Section 236 without additional assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If participating without additional assistance, household's rent shall be increased above what it would otherwise pay by the difference between market rent and the rent household would otherwise pay multiplied by a fraction: denominator = number in household; numerator = number of ineligible persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase equals market-rent differential times fraction of ineligible members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method — Section 236 with additional assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If participating with additional assistance, rent increase equals: (i) difference between market rate rent and basic rent multiplied by fraction (numerator = ineligible persons; denominator = total persons) PLUS (ii) the rent supplement/housing assistance/rental assistance otherwise payable multiplied by fraction (numerator = ineligible persons; denominator = total persons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-part calculation: market/basic rent differential prorated plus prorated share of other assistance amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method — Section 8 (non-voucher) stepwise calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Determine gross rent for the unit (contract rent plus tenant-paid utilities). Step 2: Determine total tenant payment per §5.613(a) (annual income includes income of all family members). Step 3: Subtract Step 2 from Step 1. Step 4: Multiply amount from Step 3 by fraction: numerator = number of family members with established eligible immigration status; denominator = total number of family members. The result is the prorated housing assistance payment. Proration does not affect contract rent; family pays portion not covered by prorated assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gross-rent minus tenant contribution times eligible-members fraction yields prorated payment; owner contract rent preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method — Section 8 voucher tenancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Determine pre-proration housing assistance payment (annual income includes income of all members). Step 2: Multiply pre-proration payment by fraction: numerator = number of family members with established eligible immigration status; denominator = total number of family members. The result is the prorated housing assistance payment. Proration does not affect rent to owner; family must pay portion not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voucher assistance amount is reduced by eligible-members fraction; owner rent remains unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method — Public Housing (flat rent/TTP approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Determine total tenant payment per §5.628. Step 2: Subtract total tenant payment from PHA-established flat rent applicable to unit => family maximum subsidy. Step 3: Divide family maximum subsidy by number of persons in family to determine member maximum subsidy. Step 4: Multiply member maximum subsidy by number of family members who have citizenship or eligible immigration status. Product of steps 1–4 is eligible subsidy; family's rent is flat rent minus eligible subsidy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proration uses flat rent minus prorated subsidy per eligible member; exceptions per §960.507 may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration when mixed family's TTP > public housing flat rent
rubrics_metrics.description: When mixed family's total tenant payment (TTP) is greater than the flat rent, the PHA must use the TTP as the mixed family TTP. The PHA subtracts from the mixed family TTP any established utility allowance, and the sum becomes the mixed family rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTP controls when it exceeds flat rent; utility allowance subtracted to compute mixed family rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of assistance to noncitizen students
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions permitting continued assistance or temporary deferral do not apply to any person determined to be a noncitizen student (as defined in INA §214(c)(2)(A)). The family of a noncitizen student may be eligible for prorated assistance as provided in §5.520.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibition extends to noncitizen spouse and minor children accompanying/following to join the student; it does not extend to the citizen spouse of the noncitizen student or the children of the citizen spouse and noncitizen student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with nondiscrimination and equal opportunity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entity shall administer restrictions on assisted housing by noncitizens with ineligible immigration status in conformity with all applicable nondiscrimination and equal opportunity requirements, including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (24 CFR part 1), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (24 CFR part 8), and the Fair Housing Act (24 CFR part 100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD-specific statutory and regulatory nondiscrimination obligations must be observed when applying these restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from liability for responsible entities and government agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entities are protected from liability as set forth in Section 214(e) (42 U.S.C. 1436a(e)). State and local government agencies and officials shall not be liable for design or implementation of the verification system in §5.512, so long as implementation is in accordance with prescribed HUD rules and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with HUD-prescribed rules confers liability protection for entities and officials implementing verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability of ineligible tenants for reimbursement of benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a tenant received HUD assistance to which the tenant was not entitled because the tenant intentionally misrepresented eligible status, the ineligible tenant is responsible for reimbursing HUD for the assistance improperly paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If improper assistance amount is substantial, responsible entity is encouraged to refer case to HUD Inspector General; possible criminal prosecution may follow under False Statements Act (18 U.S.C. 1001 and 1010).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart F purpose and applicability (topics covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart F states HUD requirements on: (a) determining annual and adjusted income of applicants/recipients in Section 8 and public housing; (b) determining payments by and utility reimbursements to assisted families; (c) additional occupancy requirements for Section 8 project-based assistance (income-eligibility/income-targeting, owner selection preferences, owner reexamination of family income/composition); (d) determining adjusted income for certain Section 202/811 programs; (e) limitations on eligibility based on assets as provided in §5.618.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerates the scope of regulatory rules contained in Subpart F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and standards for eligibility/calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of programmatic definitions that determine eligibility, income, deductions, and calculations, including (but not limited to) Adjusted income (§5.611), Annual income (§5.609), Child care expenses (deductible only where necessary to enable employment/education and reflect reasonable charges), Day laborer, Dependent, Disability assistance expenses (reasonable, necessary attendant care/auxiliary apparatus, not paid to family member or reimbursed), Economic self‑sufficiency program, Extremely low‑income family (poverty guideline or 30% AMI rule), Foster adult/child, Full‑time student, Health and medical care expenses, Imputed welfare income (§5.615), Independent contractor (per IRS rules), Low income family (≤80% AMI), Medical expenses, Minor, Monthly adjusted income, Monthly income, Net family assets (net cash value, include dispositions for less than fair market value within prior 2 years except certain separations; exclusions enumerated i–xi), Owner, Responsible entity (program-specific meanings for §5.611), Seasonal worker, Tenant rent, Total tenant payment (§5.628), Utility allowance, Utility reimbursement, Very low income family (≤50% AMI), Welfare assistance, and Work activities (per Social Security Act §407(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions function as binding measurement and eligibility criteria across calculations and proration rules; the net family assets entry includes an explicit list of excluded values (necessary personal property; non-necessary personal property ≤ $50,000 threshold; retirement accounts; real property family cannot sell; amounts recovered in civil actions for disability-related claims; Coverdell/529/ABLE/baby-bond accounts; interests in Indian trust land; equity in certain manufactured/homeownership assistance; FSS accounts; federal tax refunds/refundable credits for 12 months) and rules on trust funds not under family control.
